summary: Frontend e2e testing of the RST Tech Next.js marketing site. All 4 pages load (HTTP 200) with correct H1 content, navbar links route correctly, and all 8 Dream Funnel data-testid links exist with correct href (https://dreamfunnel.net), target=_blank, and rel=noopener noreferrer. Contact form UI validation works (empty submit blocked by HTML5 required). However, the contact form success flow FAILS when tested through the public preview URL because /api/contact returns HTTP 502 from Cloudflare. Root cause: this preview environment routes all /api/* requests to backend port 8001 (expected FastAPI), but this is a Next-only app that serves /api/contact from Next on port 3000. Direct localhost:3000 test of the endpoint returned HTTP 200 and Resend accepted the email (id b87b8e43-...), so the application code is correct and will work on Vercel.

integration_issues.flow: Contact form submission via public preview URL
integration_issues.issue: POST /api/contact via the preview URL returns 502 Bad Gateway (Cloudflare). Kubernetes ingress routes /api/* to backend port 8001, but this Next-only app serves the API route from Next on port 3000. On the public URL the UI stays on the form; neither contact-success nor contact-error appears within 20s. Direct test against localhost:3000 succeeds (HTTP 200, Resend email id returned), so the code is correct — this is a preview-env routing limitation. Will work correctly on Vercel.

action_items: No code changes needed for the app itself — the contact form works end-to-end on localhost (verified with curl POST returning {ok:true, id:...}) and will work on Vercel where Next.js handles all routing.

If the user wants /api/contact to be reachable through the Emergent preview URL, the preview ingress needs to route /api/* to port 3000 for this Next-only app, OR add a proxy on port 8001 that forwards to the Next server. Otherwise, verify on Vercel post-deploy.
Minor: HMR WebSocket errors (wss://.../_next/webpack-hmr 502) appear in dev console. Cosmetic only; does not affect production build on Vercel.
critical_code_review_comments: Contact API (/app/app/api/contact/route.ts) does not validate email format; only checks presence. Consider stronger validation and length caps on all fields (name is capped to 120 and message to 5000, but email is not length-capped).
No rate limiting on /api/contact — could be abused to burn Resend quota / send spam. Consider adding basic IP or session-based rate limiting before production.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All static pages, navigation, and Dream Funnel external links are verified correct. The contact form UI + client code is correct; the /api/contact Next route works when hit at localhost:3000 (verified via curl: HTTP 200, Resend id returned). The only failure mode is that /api/* is not reachable through the Emergent preview URL because the ingress expects a FastAPI backend on port 8001, which does not exist in this Next-only app. On Vercel this will work natively. If retesting, either use localhost:3000 for the API call or ensure preview routing forwards /api/* to port 3000.
rca_of_the_issue: Preview environment ingress rule maps /api/* -> port 8001 (FastAPI). This app is Next.js-only (no FastAPI); the /api/contact route is served by Next on port 3000. Therefore public POSTs to https://<preview>/api/contact hit an empty upstream and Cloudflare returns 502. Confirmed by: (1) curl to https://<preview>/api/contact returns HTTP 502; (2) curl to http://localhost:3000/api/contact returns HTTP 200 with {ok:true, id:...}; (3) no service listening on port 8001. Fix path: deploy to Vercel (intended target) where Next handles all requests, or reconfigure preview ingress to route /api/* to port 3000 for Next-only apps.
